cells.tense: The pen is in your hand today, and what you've kept steady is already moving outward.
cells.act: face one way for three days
cells.ask: Give the heading you want three days, and during them look at nothing beside it. No review of the others until the three are done.
cells.core:
The work you keep at is steady and unshowy, and it has started to leave your hands — what you built by repetition is doing something for people who didn't watch it being built. You can set what you've made in front of someone else without gripping it, and the handing over doesn't thin it. That's the shape when this runs clean: a light kept lit whether or not anyone is standing nearby, reaching past the place it was lit in.

Where you aim next doesn't need a case built for it. Commit to the heading you want and leave the others unchecked for three days; surveying them is what costs you, not the commitment. Put the pen down on the decision and pick it up on the practice. What you pass on follows from what you've honestly built, and you don't have to guard it — it wasn't made of flash.
cells.sheetLine: You can pass on what you've built without holding it tight.
cells.verb: sharing strength by measure — holding what others need and letting it go where it is needed
cells.place: a small, steady light kept lit by attention rather than by flash, in the place where you practise

cells.tense: You are already spending tomorrow's strength, and it hasn't been made yet.
cells.act: return the small thing you owe before anyone asks
cells.ask: Return one small thing you owe — a borrowed object, a return owed, a favor unpaid — quietly, before it's raised.
cells.core:
You can see who needs what, so you move toward them early — before the need has told you its size, before the timing has arrived. From outside it reads as care. What it does to you is brace: you're spending strength the practice hasn't made yet, and no amount of it feels like enough when it's measured against a future that can't be written in. The care keeps doing something for them. The speed keeps doing something to you.

What holds here is holding without forcing. Return one small thing you owe, quietly, before it's raised — not the whole account, just the next entry on it. You'll find the count ends in days rather than months, and that the items you return settle themselves; the debt that felt like a life sentence was a short list. Strength that contains rather than crushes is the shape you're after, and it begins with the smallest thing owed.

cells.tense: A door you already walked through is being stood in front of.
cells.act: engage the hard part on purpose and see what holds
cells.ask: Go at the hard part of the practice on purpose, once, and see what holds when you're inside it — no plan past that.
cells.core:
The practice has stalled, and it isn't from lack of will. The way you've been running it stopped fitting a while back — the hours are on the calendar, the motions happen, and what they were building has gone quiet. You're holding a form that no longer holds anything, which is why more effort doesn't move it. What's owed is release, and release that comes from finishing rather than quitting.

Engagement is the test, not pressure. Go at the hard part on purpose and see what holds when you're inside it — the friction will show you which way is finished and which still has weight. What survives it is what you were dedicated to; what doesn't was only the wrapping. The commitment does the pulling; the old form doesn't need defending.
cells.sheetLine: It's the method that's finished, not the commitment.

cells.tense: You are steering by something already chosen, and no account of it has been signed.
cells.act: decide the heading from what you want, not from logic
cells.ask: Decide the next heading from what you want rather than from the reasons, then take the first step that heading asks for.
cells.core:
The practice that looks steady from outside is being held — by you, by repetition — and the why of it isn't on the page. You'd say you're just doing the work, and the work is being done by someone who hasn't owned the aim. The light is lit and the place is warm, and nobody, including whoever holds the match, has said which way it's pointed. The heading is being picked below the watermark, where it can't be checked and can't be revised.

What returns this to balance is putting the choice where you can see it. Decide the next heading from what you want rather than from the reasons, then take the first step it asks for — the practice won't change shape much, it will simply belong to someone. The strength you're sharing already has a heading. The work is signing it.
cells.sheetLine: You're steering, and the choice hasn't been signed.

attempts.check: The record says exactly one thing about where this person stands — that the capacity is now aligned, or over-projected, or past-anchored, or disowned — and on that basis it does not say what the person's history with practice is. So the core never explains why this shape arose, never names a motive or a teacher or a loss. A reader could reasonably say 'you don't know my circumstances', and the cells are written so that no circumstance is needed for the claim to be usable. The asks are the medicine's own acts, small enough to be done in any room, and they do not depend on the read being right: turning toward one direction, holding a count no one sees, dropping a method that no longer fits, or putting the chosen thing where the room can see it — each teaches the person something a camera could catch even if the picture behind it is wrong. The one sentence that serves the writer here is 'this is what keeps the light steady in this way of working' — the cell does not say it; it shows the light already burning, and lets the person decide whether it is theirs.
